Extra Nos
eks´tra nōs
adv. phrase (Latin: outside of us; the location of justifying righteousness, in Christ, not in the believer's infused quality)
Latin extra, outside, beyond, + nos, us. Reformation shorthand for the alien righteousness: the righteousness by which a sinner is justified is Christ's, counted to him, not a habit poured into him.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Extra nos names where the righteousness that justifies is found: outside the sinner, in Christ. Paul will not be found in his own: “not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith” (Php 3:9). David had already sung the same location: “the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works” (Rom 4:6). The exchange is in another: “he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him” (2Co 5:21). Isaiah's picture is clothing, not infusion: “he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness” (Isa 61:10). And the verdict is free: “Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus” (Rom 3:24). In Him. Through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. Not in a quality the sinner has begun to possess. That is the whole Reformation in two Latin words.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for the Latin phrase. Extra nos is Reformation shorthand: the righteousness that justifies is Christ's, outside the sinner, imputed, not a habit infused within.

expand to see more

EXTRA NOS, Latin, outside of us. Reformation theological phrase, not an 1828 English headword.

The righteousness by which a man is justified is not in him as a poured quality. It is Christ's, counted to him.

Opposite of infused righteousness as the ground of the verdict.

Luther, Melanchthon, and the Protestant scholastics used the phrase to keep justification from sliding back into a change of the sinner's interior as its ground.

Key Scripture

Php 3:9 — "And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith:"

Rom 4:6 — "Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,"

2Co 5:21 — "For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him."

Isa 61:10 — "I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels."

Rom 3:24 — "Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:"

Modern Corruption

Rome puts the righteousness inside the man as a habit, and then the verdict waits on the habit. The gospel puts it in Christ, and the verdict is already spoken.

expand to see more

Tridentine justification is not extra nos. It is a process in which grace is infused, cooperation begins, and the man becomes formally righteous by an interior gift. Philippians 3:9 will not have two righteousnesses mixed into one ground. Paul will be found in Him, not having his own. A righteousness that is of the law, even a Spirit-assisted law-keeping, is still his own. Extra nos is the refusal of that mixture.

The evangelical corruption is quieter. Justification is still preached as a verdict, and then assurance is quietly relocated to the quality of the inner life. When a man looks at his sanctification to find out whether he is justified, he has crawled back inside himself. Romans 4:6 is blessedness without works. The robe in Isaiah 61:10 is put on him. He did not grow it.

Sanctification is real, and it is inside us. That is why the phrase has to be kept for justification. Confusing the two is how Rome and how a nervous Protestant end up in the same place: looking in the mirror for a righteousness God located in His Son.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin extra nos, outside us; Greek logizomai (G3049), to impute; dikaiosynē (G1343), righteousness; en autō, in him.

expand to see more

Latin extra nos — outside us; the Protestant scholastic location of justifying righteousness.

Greek logizomai (G3049) — to impute, count; Romans 4:6, 4:5, 4:24.

Greek en autō (G1722) — in him; 2 Corinthians 5:21, the righteousness of God in Christ, not in the sinner.

Usage

"“Not having mine own righteousness” — the man will be found in Him."

"“Imputeth righteousness without works” — outside, counted, not grown."

"“Covered me with the robe of righteousness” — put on, not infused as the verdict's ground."
